text:
Alex K: raising an escalation for a customer reporting p99 spikes + API timeouts since ~02:10UTC, they see GPU OOMs on dedicated pool
Maria T: thanks — got the tenant id and example request payload from support, sending to eng infra now
Sam R: quick note: initial SLO alert shows p50 ok, p95 up 2x, p99 up ~6x — correlates with increased KV size on that pool
Jessie L: ops-bot dropped these alerts: 
ops-bot: [ALERT] p99 latency 1.2s -> 6.8s cluster:dedicated-gpu-pool-7
ops-bot: [METRIC] gpu_mem_used_pct=92% kv_cache_bytes=18GB per-node
Alex K: customer repro steps attached: long-running chat session with repeated edits + message cancels. they ran repeated calls with conversation_id pinned.
Maria T: can you paste the short repro curl? I want to run it against a repro environment
Alex K: sure — simplified: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-opt-kv","conversation_id":"conv-123","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
then send ~200 messages in the same conversation with some cancels: `PATCH /v1/conversations/conv-123/cancel` intermittently
Sam R: ran that in a local repro VM for ~30m — KV cache grew ~500MB/min, per-GPU usable memory dropped, fragmentation increased. Eventually allocation failed and we fell back to slower-path, causing p99 jumps
Jessie L: logs from node-5 show repeated allocation failure traces (trimmed): 
```
E allocator: failed alloc 33554432 bytes, free_total=24MB, slabs: [8MB, 16MB, 0, ...]
W runtime: falling back to CPU decode path for request req-9f2
```
Infra Eng: looks like a combined effect: KV growth (per-conv state never evicted due to cancel edgecase) + allocator fragmentation -> OOMs and slow-paths.
Maria T: actionable asks: 1) short-term mitigation for customer, 2) repro-confirmed fix, 3) long-term allocator/kv fixes
Alex K: short-term mitigations we tried for customer: restart affected hosts (clears KV + free memory) and enable `kv_max_per_tenant=3GB` on pool — that reduced p99 but is manual
Sam R: also tested runtime flag `kv_evict_on_cancel=true` — with that enabled the KV growth stopped in repro, memory stabilized, p99 back to baseline
Jessie L: patch suggestion: default `kv_evict_on_cancel` to true in next rollout and add metric `kv_accumulated_by_conv` so we can alert earlier
Maria T: alternative allocator tuning: reduce slab_min_alloc to 4MB and enable aggressive coalescing on same host — reduced fragmentation in our bench, but needs careful rollout (may increase compaction CPU)
Alex K: customer is asking for a non-disruptive workaround they can apply via console or API — any quick config toggle?
Sam R: we can expose `kv_evict_on_cancel` as per-tenant feature flag in console (short rollout) — low risk, reversible
Jessie L: I'll add a canary plan: enable flag for 5% of tenant traffic in dedicated pool, monitor p99 and OOM counts for 1h
Maria T: also add automated eviction policy: if kv_bytes_per_conv > 50MB and last_active > 2h then evict oldest keys — implement as config rule
support-bot: customer update: they will accept toggle and manual host restart for now, asking for ETA on fix
Infra Eng: ETA: short-term feature flag + canary today (2h), allocator tunables and metric additions in next runtime release (2 weeks)
Alex K: repro commands and diagnostic steps I've run: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv -l 2` ; `pmap -x $(pidof runtime)` ; `./alloc_prof --sample 30s` and we pulled heap histogram showing many small free fragments
Sam R: note: when falling back to CPU decode path throughput dropped 7x which disproportionately affected p99; that's why p50 unaffected
Jessie L: follow-up items (assigned): 
- Alex K: add reproduction script and attach to ticket (#T-3492)
- Sam R: implement `kv_evict_on_cancel` quick patch + unit tests and build canary image
- Maria T: coordinate tenant feature flag rollout and inform customer
- Infra Eng: add `kv_accumulated_by_conv` metric and OOM counter alarm
Maria T: I'm pinging customer with ETA and mitigation steps now :thumbsup:
Alex K: closing loop here, will post canary results in this thread
Maria T: thanks everyone — please add any additional notes here
Sam R: initial canary shows 30m with flag on for 5% tenants -> no OOMs, kv growth flattened, p99 dropped to baseline (sending graphs shortly)
Jessie L: moving to postmortem template once fully resolved
Alex K: thx — good job team :rocket:
